title: Inspection and Maintenance Report Extraction
summary: Extract readings, observations and recommendations from test reports, NDT surveys, vendor service reports and job cards into your CMMS, with out-of-limit values flagged for engineers.

seo.title: Inspection and Maintenance Report Extraction | VipraTech
seo.description: AI that reads test reports, inspection checklists and job cards, extracts readings and recommendations, checks limits and updates your CMMS.

problem.intro: Power plants, substations, mines and refineries generate a steady flow of test and inspection reports: transformer oil and dissolved gas analysis, insulation resistance and relay tests, ultrasonic thickness surveys, lifting equipment examinations and vendor service visits. Most arrive as PDFs or scans in each vendor's format, and the readings rarely reach the asset record in a form anyone can trend.

pain_points.title: Readings locked in vendor PDFs
pain_points.detail: Each testing agency and OEM uses its own layout, so values are re-typed into spreadsheets, if they are entered at all.

pain_points.title: No trend across years
pain_points.detail: Comparing this year's oil test or insulation resistance with earlier results means digging through folders by hand.

pain_points.title: Recommendations that never close
pain_points.detail: Vendor recommendations such as oil filtration, re-tightening or replacement sit in report text with no owner or due date.

pain_points.title: Audit and inspection preparation
pain_points.detail: Finding the last valid examination report for a pressure vessel or crane before an inspection takes hours of searching.

solution.overview: We build a report pipeline that collects inspection and test documents from email, vendor portals and scanned job cards. Each report is classified by type, matched to the asset tag in your register and read by OCR with table extraction and a language model working to a schema for that report type. Readings are captured with units and test conditions, normalised, checked against acceptance limits taken from your standards and OEM manuals, and compared with the asset's previous results. Observations and recommendations become tracked action items. Uncertain values and out-of-limit flags go to an engineer, and approved data is written to the CMMS with a link to the source page.
capabilities: Classifies report types such as oil and DGA, insulation resistance, relay test, thickness survey, lifting equipment examination and vendor service report
Extracts tabular readings with units, test conditions and dates, including from scanned pages
Matches each report to the correct asset tag in the CMMS register
Checks values against configured acceptance limits and the asset's previous results
Turns vendor recommendations into action items with owners and due dates
Links every stored value to its page in the source report

workflow.title: Collect reports
workflow.detail: Reports arrive from shared mailboxes, vendor portals, scanners and mobile uploads of handwritten job cards.

workflow.title: Classify and match asset
workflow.detail: Each document is classified by report type and matched to the asset tag, using nameplate details where tags are missing.

workflow.title: Extract readings and observations
workflow.detail: OCR and an LLM extract readings, units, test conditions, observations and recommendations into the schema for that report type.

workflow.title: Validate
workflow.detail: Values are checked for confidence, acceptance limits and change against previous results.

workflow.title: Engineer review
workflow.detail: An engineer confirms uncertain values and decides on out-of-limit flags before they change the asset record.

workflow.title: Update CMMS and track actions
workflow.detail: Approved results are written to the asset record, and recommendations open as tracked actions.

inputs: Transformer oil test and dissolved gas analysis reports
Insulation resistance, polarisation index and relay test reports
Ultrasonic thickness and other NDT survey reports
Lifting equipment and pressure vessel examination reports
Vendor service reports and handwritten job cards
Asset register and acceptance limits from standards and OEM manuals
outputs: Structured test results stored against each asset
Action items from vendor recommendations with owners
Audit log of extracted values and engineer edits
human_in_the_loop: Engineers confirm uncertain values and every out-of-limit flag before the asset record changes. Decisions on outages, repairs and replacements remain with the asset owner; the system does not interpret results beyond the limits you configure.
integrations: SAP PM, IBM Maximo or another CMMS
SharePoint or a document management system
Testing laboratory and OEM vendor portals
Asset health dashboards or BI tools
guardrails: Acceptance limits come from your standards and OEM documents and are version-controlled, never generated by the model
Unit and range sanity checks before any value is stored
Every value traceable to its page in the source report
Access to vendor and asset reports controlled by role
compliance_notes: Keeps inspection and test records retrievable for statutory electrical, boiler, pressure vessel and lifting equipment inspections; the inspections themselves remain with competent persons.

pilot.scope: Two report types, such as transformer oil and DGA reports and insulation resistance tests, for one substation cluster or plant, including a backlog of past reports.
deliverables: Extraction schemas agreed with your maintenance engineers
Working pipeline on real reports from your vendors
CMMS integration plan and roll-out estimate

what_we_measure.how: Extracted values compared with values entered or verified by engineers.
Share of reports linked to the correct asset tag on a checked sample.
Values routed to engineers because of low confidence or limit failures.
Timed on a sample of reports with and without the pipeline.

faqs.q: Can it read handwritten job cards and checklists?
faqs.a: Yes for most legible handwriting, especially where the form layout is consistent. Values the model is unsure about go to an engineer rather than being guessed, and the pilot reports printed and handwritten accuracy separately.

faqs.q: Our testing vendors all use different formats. Is that a problem?
faqs.a: No. The language model reads each report in context against a schema for the report type, so a new vendor layout does not need a new template. We still test on samples from each major vendor before roll-out.

faqs.q: Will it diagnose transformer faults from DGA results?
faqs.a: No. It flags values and trends against the limits and interpretation rules you configure, and the engineer makes the diagnosis. That keeps engineering judgement with the people accountable for it.

faqs.q: How does it connect to SAP PM or Maximo?
faqs.a: Through the CMMS API or a staging table, usually writing measurement documents, notifications or attachments against the functional location or asset. We agree the exact objects with your SAP or Maximo team during the pilot.
